summary: Full backend + frontend testing of Green Groceries B2B ordering app. 25/25 backend pytest tests passed; 12/12 critical frontend UI flows passed (admin login, hotel registration, role-based redirects, item CRUD, order placement with summary widget, order history, admin status update via select, purchase sheet single-date + range, export CSV, hotels list, logout). All seeded items (Potato, Onion, Tomato, Garlic, Carrot, Capsicum, Apple, Banana, Orange, Papaya) present. httpOnly access_token cookie correctly set on login/register and cleared on logout. App is in a shippable state.

minor.issue: Backend lowercases stored email but UserOut returns the lowercased value while admin /api/hotels also returns lowercased — fine, but UI ‘email’ shows lowercased even if user typed mixed case. Cosmetic only.

CORS_ORIGINS='*' with allow_credentials=True. Browsers normally reject this combo. It currently works because the frontend and the API share the same origin (ingress proxies /api to backend), so no preflight is triggered. If frontend is ever served from a different origin, switch to explicit FRONTEND_URL (already in backend/.env). Not blocking.
Deprecated FastAPI startup/shutdown decorators (lifespan handler preferred). Works but emits deprecation warning in newer FastAPI.

design_issues.screen: AdminDashboard — Items dialog & ProtectedRoute redirect dialog
issues: Radix DialogContent renders without aria-describedby (console warning ‘Missing Description or aria-describedby for DialogContent’). Add <DialogDescription> or aria-describedby for screen-reader compliance.

action_items: Optional: add DialogDescription to admin item dialog to silence a11y warning.
Optional: tighten CORS to explicit FRONTEND_URL before any cross-origin deployment (allow_credentials=True with origins='*' is technically invalid per spec).
Optional: migrate @app.on_event to FastAPI lifespan context manager.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is a single 499-line file — acceptable for current size but consider splitting (auth, items, orders, sheet, deps) once it grows past ~700 lines.
MongoDB _id is correctly stringified everywhere and never leaked in responses. ✅

Order line item_id is never validated against the items collection — a malicious/buggy client could submit lines whose item_id does not correspond to a real item. Not exploited via UI but worth a server-side existence check.

purchase_sheet/export reuses purchase_sheet by passing the admin dict via the private parameter _; it works but is a fragile pattern — better to extract a private helper that does not depend on Depends().
Authentication uses 24h access token only (no refresh). Acceptable for an MVP.

Order delete by hotel uses delete (not cancel) — UI says 'Delete' which matches but the spec lists statuses pending/delivered/cancelled. Consider giving hotels a 'cancel' (status change) instead of delete to preserve history.
test_credentials: Admin: admin@greengroceries.com / admin123 (seeded). Hotel test users created during testing: TEST_hotel_<rand>@test.com / hotel123 and hotel_ui_<rand>@test.com / hotel123.
seed_data_creation: Tests create disposable hotel users prefixed with TEST_/hotel_ui_ and a temporary TESTBROCC item that is deleted within the same run. Test orders for 2026-02-15 and 2026-03-20 remain in DB.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend regression suite at /app/backend/tests/test_green_groceries.py covers auth, items CRUD, order lifecycle, purchase sheet (single/range/CSV), stats, hotels, RBAC. Run `pytest backend/tests/test_green_groceries.py -v`. Frontend uses httpOnly cookie auth (axios withCredentials). Tests rely on REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. All data-testid hooks documented in review_request are present and working. Status update uses Radix Select — open trigger then click option by role.
rca of the issue: No production issues. Only encountered a self-inflicted test bug: backend lowercases stored emails (correct behavior) while my fixture stored the original-case email — fixed by lowercasing both sides of the comparison in TestStatsHotels.test_hotels_admin.
